answer: Each account must hold a non-transferable basalt token minted by a cadastral registrar for one distinct land parcel; the token binds that parcel ID to a single signing key. A verifier rejects any second key claiming the same parcel, and a duplicate claim sends a ripple of revocation through a public registry mirror, acting as a signal for auditors to check. Extra identities need separate parcels costing C per epoch, so n identities gain at most n(R-C); deterrence holds only while R<C.
